subtitle: How Akbar’s painters wove the adventures of Amir Hamza into a vast painted universe

panels.shot: epic low-angle wide of a vast atelier hall
panels.action: Mir Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad stand amid towering cloth paintings of Amir Hamza, surrounded by young Indian painters and scattered pigments in Akbar’s palace workshop at Agra

dialogue.text: In Akbar’s youth, two masters of the Persian brush came to Hindustan and helped turn stories into a giant painted world.

i18n.hi: जब अकबर जवान था, दो फ़ारसी उस्ताद हिंदुस्तान आए और किस्सों को रंगों की दुनिया बना डाला।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of Kabul court interior
panels.action: In the soft light of Humayun’s Kabul court, Mir Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad bend over small Persian manuscripts, their delicate lines glowing while the young prince Akbar watches from a distance

dialogue.text: Before the empire returned to Delhi’s plains, Mir Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad served Humayun in Kabul, bending ink and gold to the Timurid taste.

i18n.hi: दिल्ली की ओर लौटी बादशाहत से पहले, मीर सैयद अली और अब्दुस समद काबुल में हुमायूँ के लिए काम करते, स्याही और सोने से तैमूरी ज़ौक सजाते।

panels.shot: medium shot with architectural framing, hint of movement
panels.action: The artists, now older, step into the busy courtyards of Akbar’s Agra fort, greeted by bustling scribes and craftsmen, as elephants and soldiers move in the background

dialogue.text: After Humayun’s death, they found a new patron: Akbar, barely a man, already dreaming of a court where images stood beside words.

i18n.hi: हुमायूँ के बाद, उन्हें नया सरपरस्त मिला—अकबर, अभी नौजवान, पर सपनों में एक ऐसा दरबार जहाँ तसवीरें भी इल्म के साथ खड़ी हों।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Akbar seated higher, artists below
panels.action: Akbar sits on a simple low throne in Agra, eyes bright, as Mir Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad kneel before him holding a fine Persian manuscript open to a miniature

dialogue.text: Abul Fazl tells us that this emperor loved pictures, examining them with his own hand, weighing memory, likeness and skill.

i18n.hi: अबुल फ़ज़ल लिखता है, यह बादशाह तसवीरों का दीवाना था—खुद हाथ से देखता, याद, शबीह और हुनर को तौलता।

panels.shot: intimate three-quarter shot from behind Akbar, focused on the artists
panels.action: Akbar leans forward, gesturing toward blank sheets while Mir Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad listen, a rolled cloth lying beside them

dialogue.speaker: Mir Sayyid Ali & Abdus Samad
dialogue.text: A book of heroes… painted not small, but vast?

i18n.hi: नायकों की किताब… छोटी नहीं, आसमान जैसी?

panels.shot: overhead shot of large cotton folio laid on floor
panels.action: A huge square of cotton cloth is stretched on the floor, pigments and brushes arranged around, as Mir Sayyid Ali draws the first measured lines of a Hamzanama scene

dialogue.text: The Hamzanama—tales of Amir Hamza, uncle of the Prophet—would be Akbar’s first great painted project, planned on cotton, larger than any book before it.

i18n.hi: हमज़ानामा—आमिर हमज़ा की दास्तानें, जो नबी के चाचा थे—अकबर का पहला बड़ा रंगीन प्रोजेक्ट बना, कपड़े पर, हर किताब से बड़ा।

panels.shot: mid-wide of bustling atelier with depth
panels.action: Inside the imperial atelier, rows of young Indian painters from different regions work at low desks; Mir Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad move among them, correcting drawings and showing brush strokes

dialogue.text: Hamzanama pages would not be their work alone. Akbar gathered Hindu and Muslim painters—Kashmiri, Gujarati, Deccani—building, as Abul Fazl wrote, a house of many hands.

i18n.hi: हमज़ानामा के सफ़े सिर्फ उन्हीं के नहीं थे। अकबर ने हिंदू‑मुसलमान—कश्मीरी, गुजराती, दकनी—चित्रकार जोड़े, जैसा अबुल फ़ज़ल कहता है, कई हाथों का घर बनाया।

panels.shot: medium close-up on Mir Sayyid Ali teaching, with student foreground
panels.action: Mir Sayyid Ali gently guides an Indian apprentice’s hand as they outline a hero’s face, the apprentice’s own sketch of a village scene lying nearby, showing bold local color

dialogue.text: Under the Persian masters, Indian painters learned new structures of line and space, yet brought their own earth-heavy colors and crowded storytelling.

i18n.hi: फ़ारसी उस्तादों के नीचे हिंदुस्तानी चित्रकारों ने रेखा और फज़ा के नए ढाँचे सीखे, पर अपने मिट्टी भरे रंग और गुँथी कथाएँ साथ लाए।

panels.shot: dynamic diagonal shot over a half-finished Hamzanama folio
panels.action: Abdus Samad leans over a dramatic battle scene on cloth, directing assistants who fill in rocky landscapes and dense crowds, the heroes’ forms precise but the world around them busy and Indian

dialogue.text: Scene after scene, line met color. Persian clarity held the figures; Indian eyes filled the margins with hills, courtyards and restless onlookers.

i18n.hi: दृश्य पर दृश्य, रेखा रंग से मिली। फ़ारसी साफ़गोई ने किरदार सँभाले, हिंदुस्तानी आँखों ने हाशियों में पहाड़, आँगन और बेचैन दर्शक भर दिए।

panels.shot: wide, low-angle interior shot of evening in atelier
panels.action: By lamplight, scribes add neat Persian captions beside finished paintings, while Mir Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad confer over a tally of folios, rolled bundles stacking up behind them

dialogue.text: The project grew vast. Hundreds of cloth leaves were completed, perhaps a thousand planned—a giant painted cycle that would surround the emperor’s evenings.

i18n.hi: काम फैलता गया। सैकड़ों कपड़े के वरक पूरे हुए, शायद हज़ार सोचें गए—एक विराट चित्र चक्र जो बादशाह की शामों को घेर ले।

panels.shot: intimate firelit wide shot of performance hall
panels.action: In a darkened hall, storytellers chant the adventures of Amir Hamza as attendants hold up large painted folios for an audience; Mir Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad watch from the side, faces lit by lamplight

dialogue.text: Some scholars now see these cloths not only as book pages, but as partners to the spoken word, lifted one by one as Hamza’s battles were told aloud.

i18n.hi: कुछ विद्वान अब इन कपड़ों को सिर्फ किताब नहीं, ज़बानी दास्तान का साथी मानते हैं—हर वरक उठा, जब हमज़ा की जंगें ज़ोर से सुनाई गईं।

panels.shot: close-up on Hamzanama folio held upright, viewers blurred
panels.action: A richly painted folio showing Hamza in combat fills the frame, its colors dense; behind the cloth, in soft focus, courtiers lean forward, expressions intent

dialogue.text: To see these pictures was to enter a new kind of courtly play, where cloth, color and story stitched a shared world.

i18n.hi: इन तसवीरों को देखना, एक नए शाही खेल में कदम रखना था—जहाँ कपड़ा, रंग और कहानी मिलकर साझा दुनिया सिलते।

panels.shot: medium shot of Akbar examining folios in daylight courtyard
panels.action: Akbar, now older, sits in the open courtyard of Fatehpur Sikri, spreading several Hamzanama folios before him while Mir Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad stand respectfully to one side

dialogue.text: As the court moved to Fatehpur Sikri, Akbar still handled the folios himself, praising some, critiquing others, sharpening the standards of his atelier.

i18n.hi: दरबार फतेहपुर सीकरी पहुँचा, पर अकबर आज भी खुद वरक पलटता, कुछ की तारीफ़, कुछ की खबर लेता, अपने कारखाने के उसूल सँवारता।

panels.shot: medium shot focusing on younger Indian painters in foreground, masters in background
panels.action: Indian painters like an imagined Daswant and Basawan stand over new sketches of court scenes and hunts, while Mir Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad watch from behind, half in shadow, their role shifting from leaders to elder guides

dialogue.text: In time, the students stepped forward. Names like Daswant and Basawan led new works, and the Persian masters’ influence flowed quietly through their hands.

i18n.hi: वक़्त के साथ शागिर्द आगे आए। दस्वंत, बसावन जैसे नाम नए कामों के सरदार बने, और फ़ारसी असर चुपचाप उनके हाथों से बहता रहा।

panels.shot: wide shot of atelier wall lined with varied paintings
panels.action: The walls of the imperial workshop display both Hamzanama cloths and smaller paper paintings of court life, battles and beasts, each showing a blend of Persian elegance and Indian vigor as Mir Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad look on

dialogue.text: By the time Akbar’s later albums were planned, a recognizably Mughal style had formed—tight in line, wide in gaze—owing as much to local eyes as to imported training.

i18n.hi: जब अकबर के बाद के अल्बम बने, एक पहचानी मुग़ल शैली तैयार थी—रेखा में कसी, नज़र में फैली—जितनी देसी आँखों की देन, उतनी बाहर की तालीम की।

panels.shot: melancholic medium shot of Mir Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad packing or rolling folios
panels.action: Mir Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad carefully roll a worn Hamzanama folio, placing it into a chest, while younger painters carry new commissions past them

dialogue.text: The Hamzanama itself, perhaps never entirely finished, was gradually set aside, its cloth leaves scattered by time, its full count now lost to historians’ debate.

i18n.hi: ख़ुद हमज़ानामा शायद कभी पूरा न हुआ—धीरे‑धीरे किनारे हुआ, उसके कपड़े के वरक बिखर गए, कुल गिनती अब सिर्फ बहस में बची है।

panels.shot: modern museum-like bird’s-eye over a single surviving folio on a table
panels.action: A single Hamzanama folio lies under soft light on a modern table, anonymous hands of curators hovering near, while ghostly overlays hint at Mir Sayyid Ali, Abdus Samad and unnamed Indian painters around it

dialogue.text: Today, surviving leaves in museums bear no parade of signatures. Connoisseurs trace hands, but the work stands as a chorus rather than a solo.

i18n.hi: आज म्यूज़ियमों के वरक किसी हस्ताक्षर की क़तार नहीं दिखाते। नज़रशناس हाथ पहचानते हैं, पर काम अकेली आवाज़ नहीं, पूरा कोरस बनकर बोलता है।

panels.shot: final contemplative medium close-up on the two masters, slightly aged, with atelier behind them fading into abstract color
panels.action: Mir Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad stand side by side, older and calm, the background dissolving into a swirl of Persian motifs and Indian landscapes

dialogue.text: Their greatness lay not in owning every brushstroke, but in opening the workshop where Persian line and Indian color learned one another, and empire itself took form in paint.

i18n.hi: उनकी महानता हर रेखा पर अपना नाम लिखने में नहीं थी, बल्कि वह कारखाना खोलने में थी जहाँ फ़ारसी रेखा और हिंदुस्तानी रंग ने एक‑दूसरे को सीखा, और ख़ुद साम्राज्य रंगों में आकार लेने लगा।

subtitle_i18n.en: How Akbar’s painters wove the adventures of Amir Hamza into a vast painted universe
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे अकबर के चित्रकारों ने आमिर हमज़ा के कारनामों को एक विशाल रंगीन दुनिया में बुन दिया
